plan.disposition: plan/plan_internal/architecture_internal: not run - the design was fixed by the operator's explicit decisions in the interview (readiness command, guided-only launch, worktree path, bounded fail-open guard) before any plan existed, so a post-hoc plan review adds nothing; the built change went through the spec, code, doubt and external code reviews instead

findings.finding: readiness await had no try/catch; a throwing check would 500 instead of failing open. FIXED: caught, treated as no verdict (readinessChecked:false); test added.
route unbounded (up to 90s) and a rejection became a 500. FIXED: maxWaitMs 30s + try/catch returning status failed; test added.
resetReadinessCache leaves an old in-flight promise able to write the cache; test-only. Accepted.
no-loop detection matches English stderr text; failure mode benign (fails open). Accepted.
failed/escalated step the scheduler reports ready gets a Launch button (retry). Intended.
20s poll per expanded card; server cache+coalescing bound cost. Accepted.

Claim under doubt: guard only refuses when a launch is illegitimate — campaign-level gates (id:null blockers: unsupported strategy / finalized) made every pending unit !ready, so the guard 409'd and the UI hid every launch path.

Claim under doubt: stale root state cannot mis-attach, guard unaffected — skipping root units for any slug with a worktree DIR blinds the double-launch guard to a live root-based run when the dir has no loop.
Claim under doubt: 15s cached verdict is safe for the guard — a cached 'waiting' refuses a launch for up to 15s after the dependency merged.
Claim under doubt: step lookup / missing unit degrade gracefully — case-only-different ids matched first hit; a step absent from the report had no launch control while the card fallback was hidden.
Claim under doubt: mirror equals contract — loop_id nullability widened vs vendored skeleton; supported vs unit.ready two sources.
Claim under doubt: symlink/slug escape-safe — no escape constructed.

When the uncached re-check before refusing fails to produce a verdict (fresh spawn times out at 10 s, throws, or returns an unavailable/failed outcome), `fresh` is `undefined` and the code evaluates `stillBlocked = fresh?.status !== "no-loop" && (!freshUnit || …)` → `true`, so the launch is refused 409 based solely on the stale cached "blocked" verdict. Decision 3 and AC-5 explicitly say fail open on timeout/unavailable; here the guard fails closed on exactly that condition. A slow `git fetch` on the re-check turns a launchable step into a hard 409.
findings.suggestion: Treat "no fresh verdict" as not-still-blocked (fail open, set `readinessChecked = false` instead of returning 409), e.g. `const stillBlocked = fresh?.status === "report" && freshUnit != null && freshUnit.state === "pending" && !freshUnit.ready && freshUnit.blocked_by.some(x => x.id !== null);

findings.finding: freshVerdict` filters only for `status === "report"`, silently converting an `unsupported-version` fresh result into `undefined` — again feeding the fail-closed path above rather than failing open with a notice.
findings.suggestion: Once the `stillBlocked` logic is inverted per the previous finding, this collapses into "no fresh verdict → launch, flag unchecked", which is the spec-correct behavior.

findings.finding: If a worktree wave unit carries neither `started_at` nor `claimed_at` (e.g. a hand-edited or older-format `loop_state.json`), `isLive(undefined, …)` is called; depending on its implementation this likely treats a genuinely live run as dead, re-enabling the hand-launch race the change is meant to close. No test covers a live-status unit with neither timestamp.
findings.suggestion: Decide explicitly (and test) the "live status, no timestamp" case — e.g. treat missing timestamps as live, or document why not.

findings.finding: The AC-5 UI-notice path for a fail-open per-unit launch is never exercised through the rendered dialog — the test only calls `uncheckedLaunchNotice` directly and asserts strings. A regression that stops passing `notice` into `CampaignLaunchDialog` (or renders it conditionally on the wrong state) would still pass. The component test acknowledges this in a comment rather than fixing it.
findings.suggestion: Add one component test: mock readiness to a report where a unit is ready, then flip the refetch to fail (stale path) or use an `unsupported-version` outcome, click Launch, and assert `campaign-step-notice-<slug>` is rendered in the dialog.

findings.finding: The two E2E tests that validate AC-1/AC-2/AC-4/AC-8 against the real scheduler are `test.skip` without `SHIPWRIGHT_LOOP_CLAIM_SCRIPT`, so CI never runs them (the ledger acknowledges this). The always-running third test only covers the stubbed degraded path. The 409 enforcement (AC-4) therefore has no always-on end-to-end coverage — only unit/router tests with injected verdicts.
findings.suggestion: Consider a CI-runnable variant with a tiny fake `loop_claim.py` fixture (a shell/python stub emitting a canned contract-shaped report) so the full route→guard→409 path runs in CI.

findings.finding: applyCampaignStepBranch` changed from sync to async. The diff updates `branch-dispatch.ts`, and `routes.ts` already awaits dispatch, so visible callers are covered — but any other callers of this exported function outside the diff (it's exported) would now silently receive a Promise and treat it as non-null truthy. Worth confirming there are none; the diff gives no evidence either way.
findings.suggestion: Grep for other importers; if any exist, they need `await`.  Checked and clean: slug/worktree path traversal is well guarded (`SLUG_PATTERN`, realpath + `isWithin`, route-level `isValidCampaignSlug`); the launch guard is server-side and bounded; AC-6 (never read root state for a worktree campaign) is implemented and tested; AC-7 cache/coalescing (15 s / 5 s error TTL, in-flight coalescing, no 3 s-poll fetch — hook polls 20 s and is `enabled`-gated) is correct; contract drift guard with the sibling monorepo is present; `dispatchLaunchBranches` correctly adds the missing `await`.

[openai] - Category: spec | Severity: high | File: `server/src/external/launch/campaign-step-branch.ts:174` — Finding: If a cached blocked verdict triggers a fresh check that times out, fails, or omits the unit, `stillBlocked` becomes true and returns 409. AC-5 requires these cases to proceed with `readinessChecked:false`. Suggestion: Return 409 only when the fresh report contains the pending unit and confirms a dependency blocker; otherwise launch with the unchecked flag.

- Category: spec | Severity: medium | File: `client/src/components/external/CampaignLaneCard.tsx:242` — Finding: The unavailable-scheduler fallback renders `CampaignStepLaunchButton` without `notice`, so its confirm dialog does not warn that readiness was not checked. Suggestion: Pass `uncheckedLaunchNotice(readiness, stale)` to the fallback button.

- Category: spec | Severity: medium | File: `client/src/components/external/CampaignDagSteps.tsx:127` — Finding: A step missing from a report can receive a per-unit Launch button merely because it is `nextPending`. That step has not been reported ready, and the dialog gets no unchecked notice because a report exists. Suggestion: Show per-unit Launch only for `unit.ready`; handle a missing row through an explicitly warned fallback.

- Category: regression | Severity: medium | File: `server/src/core/campaign-loop-state.ts:133` — Finding: A worktree directory without `loop_state.json` is absent from `worktreeSlugs`, so a stale root state can mark that worktree campaign as attached. This conflicts with the specified rule that the root state is never read for a worktree campaign and can disable hand-launch. Suggestion: Exclude every existing campaign worktree slug from root-state attachment detection, even when its state file is missing.

Overall assessment: **ship-with-fixes**. The bounded guard and UI degradation paths need correction before the launch behavior matches the specification.
